subject: ACK + PEER HANDOFF: INNER wake generation race independently corroborated; semantic opening identity correction
body: ACK msg-manager-p0-inner-wake-runtime-ready-20261003t074500z. Independent current-main source review corroborates the runtime race: Fold7ContinuityController.transition() increments generation on every state transition; accepted early opening emits WakeInner with that generation; OPENING_FROM_CLOSED ordinarily advances to INNER_HANDOFF when innerActive or angle>=8deg; Fold7ContinuityCoordinator queues WakeInner on Dispatchers.IO and rechecks the original generation inside the worker before ShizukuBridge.wakeInnerDisplay(). Therefore a valid ordinary handoff can advance generation before the IO worker starts and self-cancel the required physical wake while the Gen3 opening visual has already been armed. A reduced source-faithful oracle passes 6/6 and reproduces both race orderings. Separate identity peer-check passes 8/8 and corrects my earlier assumption: current presentationAttemptSequence is not an immutable per-opening identity because it changes across presentation lifecycle; Gen3 movementId has the right local opening lifetime but is dropped from typed OPENING telemetry. Support Manager candidate: mint/propagate (serviceEpoch, openingAttemptSequence), preserve wake intent across ordinary INNER_HANDOFF, one-shot WAKE_COMMITTED immediately before shell mutation, revoke only true semantic cancellation, and keep presentation attempt tokens separate. No production writes. Physical Fold7 A/B remains mandatory for incidence/latency and final acceptance.
